currentContext.business: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Limited (Sona Comstar), incorporated in 1995 as a JV between Sona Group and Mitsubishi Materials, designs, manufactures and supplies highly engineered, mission-critical, complex and bespoke driveline systems (differential gears/assemblies), motors and motor sub-assemblies, and mmWave radar sensing/perception solutions for global automotive OEMs across conventional and electric passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, off-highway vehicles and electric two- and three-wheelers. In 2025 it entered the railway sector by acquiring the Railway Business of Escorts Kubota, adding brake systems, dampers, couplers and friction products. It operates 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities across India, the US, Mexico and China, with 49% of sales from international markets and about 77% of revenue from direct supplies to global OEMs.

Motors: integrated motor controller modules for active suspension systems
Sensing: perception solutions (in-cabin sensing, short-range radar) via NOVELIC

currentContext.strengths: Global scale and leadership in precision driveline systems — 8.7% global market share in differential gears and 4.2% in starter motors (CY2025)|Pioneer of precision-formed bevel gear technology in India; inventor lineage via acquired ThyssenKrupp BLW business|Deep, direct OEM relationships — ~77% of revenue from direct supplies to global OEMs across India, North America, Europe and Asia|Diversified revenue base across geographies, products, vehicle segments and customers — top-8 products now spread the revenue concentration that the top-4 products previously carried (86% in FY24-25)|R&D depth — five R&D centres and technology spanning drivetrain systems, EV motors, mmWave radar/perception (via NOVELIC) and railway safety-critical systems|Global manufacturing footprint (12 facilities across India, US, Mexico and China) supporting proximity to customers and international sales (49% of sales international)|Strong revenue visibility from a large net order book (INR 237 billion / ~USD 2.5 billion), ~70% EV-linked|Track record of platform diversification into adjacent mobility (railways via Escorts Kubota acquisition; robotics/cobots via Neura Robotics collaboration)
currentContext.strategies: Electrification: central strategic bet — building EV driveline systems, traction/suspension motors and differential assemblies for global EV programmes|Global market significance: sustaining/growing global market share in differential gears and starter motors as the yardstick of world-class competitiveness|Diversification: broadening revenue across geographies (the 'Look East' strategy toward India and China), products and customers to reduce concentration risk|Technology: continued investment in R&D, engineering capability and new product commercialisation — motors/controllers, radar sensing via NOVELIC, and railway systems|Broadening beyond automotive into railways (brakes, couplers, suspension systems, friction/rubber products) and adjacent mobility technology (robots, cobots, humanoids via a Neura Robotics collaboration)|Stated ambition to build 'an Indian product engineering company that the world can be proud of', evolving from automotive technology to broader mobility technology|The Board recommended, and shareholders were to consider, a final dividend of INR 1.80 per equity share (face value INR 10) for FY2025-26; no separate dividend-policy philosophy narrative is included in this bundle. Non-Executive Directors' aggregate commission is capped at 1% of net profits per annum, with an overall annual cap of INR 70,000,000, for a 5-year period from FY2026-27, indicating a bounded approach to non-operating profit distribution. Employee-linked equity instruments (ESOP-2023 option grants and the new Performance Share Plan 2025 tied to consolidated EBITDA growth) are used alongside dividends as tools for value distribution/retention aligned to performance.
currentContext.expansion: In the beginning of FY2025-26, the Company integrated the acquired Railway Business into its technology roadmap; it holds a leadership position in railway braking systems in India and is among the leading suppliers of couplers, dampers and friction products. During the year it commercialised three new products: a Hydraulic Motor Controller (a compact electromechanical solution for farm-equipment lifting, steering, braking and auxiliary functions), a Railway Electric Control Panel (developed for locomotives, with planned expansion into metro and modern trainsets), and a Railway HVAC System (climate control for locomotives, metro and semi-high-speed trains). The Company is also developing next-generation railway technologies and air springs for modern coaches to strengthen its position in premium and high-speed rail platforms, and expects growth from the expansion of dedicated freight corridors, metro rail networks and programmes such as Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat — spanning legacy product lines (suspension, braking, coupling) as well as newer ones (control panels, HVAC, electronic braking and suspension systems). Beyond railways, the Company signed an MoU with Neura Robotics (Germany) covering cognitive robotics and autonomous systems, establishing Robotics as a new vertical, and flagged interest in inorganic growth opportunities in semiconductors, data centres, and charging/energy infrastructure — domains where it currently has no legacy presence. This expansion is underpinned by an innovation framework built on Technology Readiness Level (TRL) methodology and digital engineering tools (systems engineering, virtual validation, CI/CD-based software development), alongside a long-term AI implementation roadmap covering forecasting/optimisation, agentic AI and digital-twin-based design augmentation.

EBITDA margin held resilient at 24.7% despite commodity and inflation headwinds|CY2026 outlook flagged as cautious given affordability pressures, tariff uncertainty and geopolitical tensions (e.g. Strait of Hormuz) that could weigh on demand and cost stability|Secured orders worth INR 57 billion during FY2025-26, taking the net order book to INR 237 billion (~USD 2.5 billion), with ~70% contribution from EV programmes|67 EV programmes across 35 customers, up from 15 five years ago, after nine new EV programme wins and three new customers added in FY2025-26|Notable programme wins included an INR 15.5 billion order for differential assemblies with final drive gear for a new EV passenger vehicle platform (a traditional North American OEM) and two nominations worth INR 8.2 billion for integrated motor controller modules for active suspension systems (an Asian EV OEM and a European luxury performance OEM)|Other wins spanned traction motors for an Indian electric three-wheeler, the first order for the Company's Mexico driveline plant (a North American recreational off-highway vehicle OEM), differential gears/assemblies for European OEMs on BEV platforms, EV differential assemblies for Indian and European OEMs, and a hybrid-platform programme

risks.note: Performance is closely linked to the global automotive sector across North America, Europe, India and Asia (excluding India); operations spanning multiple countries expose the Company to changes in legal, regulatory, tariff and trade environments, protectionist policies and logistics disruptions that could hit customer demand, supply chains and costs.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and critical-material availability
risks.note: The automotive/mobility supply chain remains vulnerable to disruption from geopolitical action, logistics bottlenecks and sudden demand shifts; availability of critical inputs (energy, rare-earth materials, electronic components, specialised raw materials) can affect production schedules and deliveries. This materialised in FY2025-26 when China's export controls on heavy rare-earth magnets created uncertainty across the EV supply chain and threatened traction-motor production, requiring an emergency motor-architecture redesign within four weeks.

Commodity price fluctuations can significantly affect manufacturing costs; despite monitoring/management mechanisms, it is not always possible to fully predict, hedge or pass through price volatility, which can pressure overall profitability.

COVID-19 demonstrated the potential for global health crises to disrupt operations and cause economic downturns; a recurrence of such a crisis could substantially affect the Company's financial condition and operations.

risks.risk: Regulatory change and the ICE-to-EV transition
risks.note: The industry is subject to stringent and evolving environmental/regulatory standards; the ongoing transition from ICE-based vehicles to electrified alternatives poses a structural risk to the Company's ICE-dependent product lines.

Customer-specific volatility (alongside tariff/trade uncertainty and inflationary pressure) affected demand visibility and production planning during FY2025-26, underscoring reliance on the mix and behaviour of a concentrated set of large OEM/Tier-1 customers.

thesis: Antifragile, diversified precision-mobility supplier that emerges stronger from disorder. Q4 FY26 was the best-ever quarter on revenue, EBITDA, PAT, BEV revenue and BEV mix (39%). Electrification momentum has decisively turned back up (EU BEV +45% YoY in March; India EV cars +65%, 2W +45%), and Sona is positioned to capture share as European EV-supplier supply chains reset. Growth engines now broaden beyond legacy diff gears to traction/suspension motors, ADAS sensors, and a fast-scaling railway business.

Q4 margin bridge: -2.7pp incl. -1.9pp base effect (PLI accrued fully in Q4 LY) + -0.8pp mix/commodity (≈50/50 split; commodity is pass-through with a lag).
guidance:
- EBITDA margin band reset to **23–25%** (was 24–26% pre-railway), expected to hold.
- Commodity inflation (steel/aluminium/copper + freight/energy) to keep pressuring % margins while prices rise; absolute margin less impacted; "no idea" when commodity cycle normalizes.
- Suspension motor = fastest-growing product (3–4x / triple-digit growth; single-digit % of rev this year, "maybe double digits" next year).
- Traction motor = second-fastest (already ~10% of rev; very high double-digit growth).
- Railways: no annual guidance; "good healthy growth" over next 3–5 yrs, new products meaningful from year 3.
- Robotics/eVTOL: meaningful revenue only beyond a 3-year horizon.
order book: Net order book ₹237 bn, EV = 70%. FY26: won 31 new programs, added 3 new customers. Q4: 4 new driveline orders (3 from European OEMs — most-ever from Europe in a quarter, first EU EV win in ~4 yrs; 1 hybrid platform). EV order book: +3 EV programs +1 hybrid +2 new EV customers → 67 EV programs / 35 customers (37 in production, 30 pre-production). Q4 non-EV: 7 diff-gear programs (existing customers, ₹3 bn add) plus starter-motor & railway wins. 100% of order book has volume visibility & pricing stability (volumes indicative, discounted by mgmt judgement).
segment: Fastest sequential growth: traction & suspension motors, then diff assemblies and diff gears (legacy "old horses" still growing). India now >50% of FY mix; "Look East" — Eastern markets 60% of Q4 rev (vs 40% YoY). Product diversification: top-4 products were 86% of rev LY; same 86% now spread across top-8 products. Railway: added electric panels (supplied first batch for locos) + HVAC (supplies start this quarter), beyond brakes/couplers.
growth: EV: BEV mix at record 39% despite US EV -28% YoY in Q4 — proves no single-market/customer dependence. Suspension motor riding a successful customer model launch (Clear Motion), strong China + Europe acceptance. Novelic ADAS: India entity set up, SOP end-CY26, EU in-cabin NCAP requirement moved to CY27. Railway TAM: HVAC ₹2,000–2,500 cr, electric panels ₹1,500 cr; full rolling-stock coverage takes 18 mo–3 yrs per product. New-product cycle is structurally ~4–5 yrs (0–3 yrs loss-making, year 4 first revenue).
margins: FY EBITDA 24.7% despite consolidating lower-margin railway and high-growth lower-margin traction motors. Pressure from product mix (motors dilutive) + commodity lag + minimum-wage hike (Haryana, eff 1-Apr-26) + higher fixed costs. Mitigation: productivity, headcount discipline, ~20% gas-requirement cut (shift to electric heating) with zero production loss. Railways dilutive to margin but accretive to ROCE/returns.
capex: FY26 capex ₹369 cr; OCF ₹659 cr → FCF ₹290 cr. ~₹1,800 cr deployed on railway business acquisition; +₹110 cr land; final Novelic tranche paid. Capital-allocation philosophy stresses **fungible capex** (e.g. 1mn electric-motor capacity usable across customers) over model-specific lines. Fixed-asset turnover dipped to 2.9 on new capitalization/land — expected to improve as FY27 revenue ramps.
capital allocation: ₹1,269 cr cash, strongest-ever balance sheet → optionality to invest while peers constrained. Dividend ₹200 cr paid FY26. M&A: always evaluating (>100 opportunities in 3 yrs, acted on 1); cash "not to burn"; four filters — 15-yr product life, top-5 market position, strong financial returns, good for humanity. No reportable M&A in pipeline.
risks: Commodity inflation + freight/energy/petrochem-linked cost rise (pass-through lag). Haryana minimum-wage hike. Gas availability (largely mitigated). Model discontinuation risk (lost ₹300 cr from one customer last year). US Section 232 tariffs unchanged at 25% (tariffs paid by importers); secondary demand hit — US SAAR ~16–16.5mn, ~1mn cars lost to inflationary impact. China "China-for-China" supply chain hard to enter. EV subsidy roll-back (e.g. BYD) — low risk as orders sit in low/no-subsidy geographies. Rare-earth/heavy magnets — Sona uses none in its products.
mgmt tone: Confident, candid, contrarian. Calls FY26 "a tough year" (Q1 lows, loss of founder Sunjay, US tariffs, magnet ban) yet delivered record Q4; "antifragility thesis playing out." Dismissed an external sell-side note (8-Apr) projecting EBITDA dropping 25%→12.5% as "half-baked and uninformed." Reframes EV "noise" as "signal." High conviction on electrification policy push over next 18 months.
non-obvious:
- European EV-supplier bankruptcies are converting into Sona order wins ("antifragility"); 3rd distressed asset acquired by a competitor — Sona pursuing customers directly.
- Hybrid wins reinforce "hybrids are an opportunity not a risk" — powertrain-agnostic positioning.
- Neura Robotics MoU opens humanoid/AMR optionality (long-dated).
- Railway is margin-dilutive but ROCE/ROE-accretive; finance income substituted by operating returns as cash deployed.
- Macro read: India energy mix ~80% fossil / 20% electric → mgmt expects strong electrification policy push (currency weakness tied to oil/gas import dependence).

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of the world's leading mobility technology companies, designing, manufacturing and supplying highly engineered, mission-critical, complex driveline, motor and sensing systems for global automotive OEMs, with an expanding presence in railways.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Limited (Sona Comstar), incorporated in 1995 as a JV between Sona Group and Mitsubishi Materials, designs, manufactures and supplies highly engineered, mission-critical, complex and bespoke driveline systems (differential gears/assemblies), motors and motor sub-assemblies, and mmWave radar sensing/perception solutions for global automotive OEMs across conventional and electric passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, off-highway vehicles and electric two- and three-wheelers. In 2025 it entered the railway sector by acquiring the Railway Business of Escorts Kubota, adding brake systems, dampers, couplers and friction products. It operates 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities across India, the US, Mexico and China, with 49% of sales from international markets and about 77% of revenue from direct supplies to global OEMs.

segment_detail.title: Segment
segment_detail.body: Fastest sequential growth: traction & suspension motors, then diff assemblies and diff gears (legacy "old horses" still growing). India now >50% of FY mix; "Look East" — Eastern markets 60% of Q4 rev (vs 40% YoY). Product diversification: top-4 products were 86% of rev LY; same 86% now spread across top-8 products. Railway: added electric panels (supplied first batch for locos) + HVAC (supplies start this quarter), beyond brakes/couplers.

order_book.title: Order book
order_book.body: Net order book ₹237 bn, EV = 70%. FY26: won 31 new programs, added 3 new customers. Q4: 4 new driveline orders (3 from European OEMs — most-ever from Europe in a quarter, first EU EV win in ~4 yrs; 1 hybrid platform). EV order book: +3 EV programs +1 hybrid +2 new EV customers → 67 EV programs / 35 customers (37 in production, 30 pre-production). Q4 non-EV: 7 diff-gear programs (existing customers, ₹3 bn add) plus starter-motor & railway wins. 100% of order book has volume visibility & pricing stability (volumes indicative, discounted by mgmt judgement).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body:
- EBITDA margin band reset to **23–25%** (was 24–26% pre-railway), expected to hold.
- Commodity inflation (steel/aluminium/copper + freight/energy) to keep pressuring % margins while prices rise; absolute margin less impacted; "no idea" when commodity cycle normalizes.
- Suspension motor = fastest-growing product (3–4x / triple-digit growth; single-digit % of rev this year, "maybe double digits" next year).
- Traction motor = second-fastest (already ~10% of rev; very high double-digit growth).
- Railways: no annual guidance; "good healthy growth" over next 3–5 yrs, new products meaningful from year 3.
- Robotics/eVTOL: meaningful revenue only beyond a 3-year horizon.

growth_optionality.title: Growth
growth_optionality.body: EV: BEV mix at record 39% despite US EV -28% YoY in Q4 — proves no single-market/customer dependence. Suspension motor riding a successful customer model launch (Clear Motion), strong China + Europe acceptance. Novelic ADAS: India entity set up, SOP end-CY26, EU in-cabin NCAP requirement moved to CY27. Railway TAM: HVAC ₹2,000–2,500 cr, electric panels ₹1,500 cr; full rolling-stock coverage takes 18 mo–3 yrs per product. New-product cycle is structurally ~4–5 yrs (0–3 yrs loss-making, year 4 first revenue).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global light vehicle sales expected to decline 1.6% year-on-year in CY2026 (per S&P Global Mobility), driven by tariff-related cost pressures, affordability challenges, elevated interest rates, softer consumer sentiment and subsidy changes in key markets
- Electrification expected to continue gaining share despite the softer overall volume outlook — IEA projects global electric car sales reaching 23 million units in CY2026, representing 28% of total car sales
- Company will continue to invest in research and development, engineering capability and technology partnerships, anchored in its four strategic priorities: electrification, global market significance, diversification and technology
- India expected to remain the world's fastest-growing major economy, with GDP growth projected in the range of 6.5%-6.6% in FY2026-27 (World Bank estimate), supporting India-led demand
- FY2025-26 revenue growth driven by new products, customer wins and railway business consolidation; EBITDA margin held resilient at 24.7% despite commodity and inflation headwinds
- CY2026 outlook flagged as cautious given affordability pressures, tariff uncertainty and geopolitical tensions (e.g. Strait of Hormuz) that could weigh on demand and cost stability
- Secured orders worth INR 57 billion during FY2025-26, taking the net order book to INR 237 billion (~USD 2.5 billion), with ~70% contribution from EV programmes
- 67 EV programmes across 35 customers, up from 15 five years ago, after nine new EV programme wins and three new customers added in FY2025-26
- Notable programme wins included an INR 15.5 billion order for differential assemblies with final drive gear for a new EV passenger vehicle platform (a traditional North American OEM) and two nominations worth INR 8.2 billion for integrated motor controller modules for active suspension systems (an Asian EV OEM and a European luxury performance OEM)
- Other wins spanned traction motors for an Indian electric three-wheeler, the first order for the Company's Mexico driveline plant (a North American recreational off-highway vehicle OEM), differential gears/assemblies for European OEMs on BEV platforms, EV differential assemblies for Indian and European OEMs, and a hybrid-platform programme

margins.title: Margins
margins.body: FY EBITDA 24.7% despite consolidating lower-margin railway and high-growth lower-margin traction motors. Pressure from product mix (motors dilutive) + commodity lag + minimum-wage hike (Haryana, eff 1-Apr-26) + higher fixed costs. Mitigation: productivity, headcount discipline, ~20% gas-requirement cut (shift to electric heating) with zero production loss. Railways dilutive to margin but accretive to ROCE/returns.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: ₹1,269 cr cash, strongest-ever balance sheet → optionality to invest while peers constrained. Dividend ₹200 cr paid FY26. M&A: always evaluating (>100 opportunities in 3 yrs, acted on 1); cash "not to burn"; four filters — 15-yr product life, top-5 market position, strong financial returns, good for humanity. No reportable M&A in pipeline.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: In the beginning of FY2025-26, the Company integrated the acquired Railway Business into its technology roadmap; it holds a leadership position in railway braking systems in India and is among the leading suppliers of couplers, dampers and friction products. During the year it commercialised three new products: a Hydraulic Motor Controller (a compact electromechanical solution for farm-equipment lifting, steering, braking and auxiliary functions), a Railway Electric Control Panel (developed for locomotives, with planned expansion into metro and modern trainsets), and a Railway HVAC System (climate control for locomotives, metro and semi-high-speed trains). The Company is also developing next-generation railway technologies and air springs for modern coaches to strengthen its position in premium and high-speed rail platforms, and expects growth from the expansion of dedicated freight corridors, metro rail networks and programmes such as Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat — spanning legacy product lines (suspension, braking, coupling) as well as newer ones (control panels, HVAC, electronic braking and suspension systems). Beyond railways, the Company signed an MoU with Neura Robotics (Germany) covering cognitive robotics and autonomous systems, establishing Robotics as a new vertical, and flagged interest in inorganic growth opportunities in semiconductors, data centres, and charging/energy infrastructure — domains where it currently has no legacy presence. This expansion is underpinned by an innovation framework built on Technology Readiness Level (TRL) methodology and digital engineering tools (systems engineering, virtual validation, CI/CD-based software development), alongside a long-term AI implementation roadmap covering forecasting/optimisation, agentic AI and digital-twin-based design augmentation.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Confident, candid, contrarian. Calls FY26 "a tough year" (Q1 lows, loss of founder Sunjay, US tariffs, magnet ban) yet delivered record Q4; "antifragility thesis playing out." Dismissed an external sell-side note (8-Apr) projecting EBITDA dropping 25%→12.5% as "half-baked and uninformed." Reframes EV "noise" as "signal." High conviction on electrification policy push over next 18 months.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Global scale and leadership in precision driveline systems — 8.7% global market share in differential gears and 4.2% in starter motors (CY2025)
- Pioneer of precision-formed bevel gear technology in India; inventor lineage via acquired ThyssenKrupp BLW business
- Deep, direct OEM relationships — ~77% of revenue from direct supplies to global OEMs across India, North America, Europe and Asia
- Diversified revenue base across geographies, products, vehicle segments and customers — top-8 products now spread the revenue concentration that the top-4 products previously carried (86% in FY24-25)
- R&D depth — five R&D centres and technology spanning drivetrain systems, EV motors, mmWave radar/perception (via NOVELIC) and railway safety-critical systems
- Global manufacturing footprint (12 facilities across India, US, Mexico and China) supporting proximity to customers and international sales (49% of sales international)
- Strong revenue visibility from a large net order book (INR 237 billion / ~USD 2.5 billion), ~70% EV-linked
- Track record of platform diversification into adjacent mobility (railways via Escorts Kubota acquisition; robotics/cobots via Neura Robotics collaboration)

risks.title: Risks
risks.body: Commodity inflation + freight/energy/petrochem-linked cost rise (pass-through lag). Haryana minimum-wage hike. Gas availability (largely mitigated). Model discontinuation risk (lost ₹300 cr from one customer last year). US Section 232 tariffs unchanged at 25% (tariffs paid by importers); secondary demand hit — US SAAR ~16–16.5mn, ~1mn cars lost to inflationary impact. China "China-for-China" supply chain hard to enter. EV subsidy roll-back (e.g. BYD) — low risk as orders sit in low/no-subsidy geographies. Rare-earth/heavy magnets — Sona uses none in its products.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- European EV-supplier bankruptcies are converting into Sona order wins ("antifragility"); 3rd distressed asset acquired by a competitor — Sona pursuing customers directly.
- Hybrid wins reinforce "hybrids are an opportunity not a risk" — powertrain-agnostic positioning.
- Neura Robotics MoU opens humanoid/AMR optionality (long-dated).
- Railway is margin-dilutive but ROCE/ROE-accretive; finance income substituted by operating returns as cash deployed.
- Macro read: India energy mix ~80% fossil / 20% electric → mgmt expects strong electrification policy push (currency weakness tied to oil/gas import dependence).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Electrification: central strategic bet — building EV driveline systems, traction/suspension motors and differential assemblies for global EV programmes
- Global market significance: sustaining/growing global market share in differential gears and starter motors as the yardstick of world-class competitiveness
- Diversification: broadening revenue across geographies (the 'Look East' strategy toward India and China), products and customers to reduce concentration risk
- Technology: continued investment in R&D, engineering capability and new product commercialisation — motors/controllers, radar sensing …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisitions] The deck attributes Phase-4 to the acquisition of NOVELIC and the Railway Business, and states "New products added inorganically contribute >40% of our current revenue"; the Railway business is led by Mr. Amit Mishra, Head, Railway Business.
- [Control change] The 4-wheeler DENSO JV moves management control to DENSO (51%), a structural change from Sona Comstar's own consolidation, while the 2/3-wheeler JV keeps Sona Comstar at 51% with control.
- [Orderbook definition] Net order book is defined as aggregate revenue from awarded programmes yet to start production or yet to fully ramp up over the next 10 years, after adjusting for programmes expected to reach end of life or be phased out and after applying a discount for unforeseen delays; the Railway order book is instead based on purchase orders to be executed largely within the next 12 months.
- [Mix labels lost] The Q1 FY27 / FY26 revenue-mix slide's "By Product" and "By Geography" percentage series could not be reliably bound to their category labels in the text extraction, so those splits are not asserted here.
